title: A Wreck for the Escarpment
premise: Marguerite Zhou, a debt-ridden storm chaser, is hired to deliver concession permits and radio equipment to an expedition surveying the Kessing Escarpment upriver. When the team goes silent, she and her crew push into monsoon country aboard a leaking boat, guided by Ilse, a river pilot with a forged identity and a history with the mining company behind the permits. As the monsoon closes in, Marguerite discovers the expedition wasn't lost—it was silenced, because its lead scientist found evidence the concession was built on falsified surveys, and the 'optimists' who hold Marguerite's debt are the company's enforcers. Torn between loyalty to her crew, who need her to deliver the permits, and the truth Ilse is risking everything to expose, Marguerite must choose. In the climax, she broadcasts the falsified surveys during the storm's eye, sacrificing the boat and nearly her life; the expedition's surviving members are rescued, the concession collapses in scandal, her debt dies with the company's fixers, and Marguerite—having finally stopped running—stays through the dry season to help rebuild the river station, measuring life in years at last.
about_author: Paloma Brightwater is the pen name of a former hydrographic surveyor who spent six seasons on tropical rivers before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people whose professions demand they read the weather better than they read each other.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. In a coastal garage, she recalibrates anemometers while dodging calls from Voss, the man who holds her debt, and accepts a delivery contract upriver. Establishes her habit of measuring everything in distance. Beat: restless competence masking dread.

chapters.title: The Optimists
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She meets Voss and his cheerful associates, who 'invest in people,' and signs papers she doesn't fully read. The permits and a radio crate are sealed for the Kessing expedition. Beat: the trap closing with a smile.

chapters.title: Crew of the Tern
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She assembles her small crew: Dez, a superstitious mechanic, and Okonjo, a young navigator who idolizes her. The boat Tern is patched and loaded. Beat: found-family warmth before the fall.

chapters.title: Ilse at the Locks
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. At the first river locks, a stranger named Ilse barges her way aboard as pilot-for-hire, knowing the escarpment reach intimately—and knowing too much about the concession. Beat: suspicion sharpened by necessity.

chapters.title: Dead Air on Channel Nine
chapters.summary: Okonjo's POV. Nightly radio checks with the Kessing expedition go unanswered. Marguerite decides to push on rather than turn back—the debt won't allow it. Beat: first true unease.

chapters.title: The Company's Reach
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse privately recognizes the permit seals as Halvern Consolidated's, the company that erased her identity and her brother. She conceals this from the crew. Beat: guilt and calculation.

chapters.title: Rising Water
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. The monsoon arrives early; the Tern takes on water through a seam Dez can't fully fix. Rations are recalculated. Beat: the river turning from road to adversary.

chapters.title: The Abandoned Camp
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. They find the expedition's forward camp—tents slashed, instruments gone, a survey ledger page half-burned showing impossible elevation figures. Beat: dread hardening into certainty.

chapters.title: Someone Is Following
chapters.summary: Okonjo's POV. Okonjo spots a fast launch trailing them through the fog; it vanishes when challenged. Ilse lies smoothly about knowing who it might be. Beat: paranoia among allies.

chapters.title: Voss on the Line
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A satellite call: Voss, too cheerful, reminds her the permits expire in eleven days and that 'investments expect returns.' She realizes he knows the expedition is silent. Beat: the debt revealed as a leash.

chapters.title: What Ilse Knows
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Confronted by Marguerite over the burned ledger, Ilse admits Halvern's surveys are forged and the expedition's lead, Dr. Amara Kessing, found proof. She withholds her personal history. Beat: half-trust established.

chapters.title: The Gorge Transit
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. A white-knuckle run through the gorge rapids in rising water; the Tern cracks a plank, Okonjo nearly goes overboard, and Ilse's piloting saves them. Beat: earned respect for the stranger.

chapters.title: The Middle Station
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. They reach a derelict river station and find Dr. Kessing's deputy, Fen, hiding—wounded, the sole survivor of an 'inspection' that turned violent. Beat: the silence explained; the stakes made flesh.

chapters.title: Fen's Account
chapters.summary: Fen's POV. Fen recounts how Halvern's men seized the survey data and scattered the team into the bush; Kessing went upstream to the escarpment itself to re-verify the readings. Beat: a mission redefined—deliver truth, not permits.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite calculates: delivering the permits saves her crew and clears her debt; destroying them saves the river and ruins them all. She chooses to keep moving upstream, telling no one her real plan. Beat: the central choice seeded.

chapters.title: The Pursuit Closes
chapters.summary: Okonjo's POV. The trailing launch reappears with company men aboard, ordering the Tern to heave to. Ilse runs the boat into a flooded side-channel to escape. Beat: no more pretending this is a delivery.

chapters.title: Stranded in the Green
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. The side-channel dead-ends in drowned forest; the Tern is wedged and holed. The crew camps on a termite mound island, bailing and bickering. Beat: exhaustion and friction.

chapters.title: Ilse's Brother
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Around the campfire, Ilse finally tells the whole truth: her name is forged, her brother died auditing Halvern's escarpment surveys, and she has been hunting proof for six years. Beat: the stranger becomes one of them.

chapters.title: The Repair
chapters.summary: Dez and Okonjo's POV. Improvising a patch from sailcloth and resin, the crew refloats the Tern through a night of lightning work. Marguerite watches her crew choose each other. Beat: battered solidarity.

chapters.title: The Eye of the Monsoon
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A freak lull—the monsoon's eye—gives them a clear window to reach the escarpment. Marguerite quietly packs the permits and the ledger page together. Beat: calm that feels like held breath.

chapters.title: The Escarpment Road
chapters.summary: Okonjo's POV. They haul the Tern up a tributary toward the base of the escarpment, passing drowned villages that accepted Halvern money and now stand empty. Beat: the cost of the concession made visible.

chapters.title: Company Men
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Halvern's launch corners them at a bend; Voss himself is aboard. He offers Marguerite debt forgiveness for the permits and Ilse's capture. She stalls. Beat: temptation offered in a friendly voice.

chapters.title: The Refusal
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite refuses, and the launch opens fire as the Tern slips into a cave channel behind the falls. Dez is grazed; the radio is damaged. Beat: the point of no return.

chapters.title: Behind the Falls
chapters.summary: Fen's POV. Hidden in the cave, they find Kessing's field camp—her instruments, her verified data proving the falsified surveys—and a note pointing to the summit relay tower. Beat: the weapon found; the way marked.

chapters.title: The Climb
chapters.summary: Okonjo's POV. The crew climbs the escarpment's goat path in the returning rain, carrying the data and a salvaged transmitter, leaving the crippled Tern behind. Beat: leaving the river, entering the vertical.

chapters.title: Kessing Alive
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Near the summit they find Dr. Amara Kessing, feverish but alive, guarded by two loyal team members who nearly shoot them. Marguerite talks them down with Fen as witness. Beat: the expedition's silence finally broken.

chapters.title: What the Surveys Prove
chapters.summary: Kessing's POV. Kessing explains: the escarpment's geology makes the concession unworkable without catastrophic damming; Halvern knew, falsified the surveys, and planned to cash out on subsidies. Beat: the truth given its full, terrible shape.

chapters.title: Voss's Last Offer
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Via the damaged radio, Voss offers everything—debt cleared, crew paid, Ilse's record wiped—in exchange for the data. Marguerite, for the first time in twenty years, measures something in years instead of miles. Beat: the temptation answered.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. In a storm lull, they reach the relay tower and Ilse transmits Kessing's data on every channel, naming names, as the company men begin climbing below. Beat: the truth loosed and irretrievable.

chapters.title: The Tower Fight
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. Halvern's men storm the tower; Dez and Okonjo hold the stairwell while the transmission completes. Dez is badly hurt; Voss's launch is wrecked by the storm surge below. Beat: the climax's violence—loyalty spent defending truth.

chapters.title: The River Answers
chapters.summary: Okonjo's POV. The broadcast is picked up by downstream stations, the port authority, and a journalist; Halvern's own surveyors confirm the forgery on air. The company men retreat. Beat: the world turning.

chapters.title: Descent in Flood
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. They carry the wounded Dez down the escarpment as the monsoon peaks, the river now a brown ocean swallowing the tributary. Beat: survival as collective act.

chapters.title: The Tern's End
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. They find the Tern shattered on the rocks. Dez, delirious, apologizes to the boat. They salvage the radio crate—the original delivery—and let the rest go. Beat: grief for the vessel that carried them.

chapters.title: The Rescue
chapters.summary: Fen's POV. A port authority patrol launch, tipped by the broadcast, reaches them at dawn. Voss is taken into custody at the locks; his 'optimists' scatter. Beat: the machinery of consequence arriving.

chapters.title: Debts and Ledgers
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. With Halvern collapsed, Marguerite's debt is void—but so is her livelihood. Kessing offers her a post running the rebuilt middle river station. Marguerite hesitates at the idea of staying anywhere. Beat: the old identity loosening.

chapters.title: Ilse's Name
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse files to reclaim her real name and registers her brother's audit findings posthumously in the inquiry. Marguerite stands witness for her. Beat: identity restored, not assumed.

chapters.title: Dry Season
chapters.summary: Okonjo's POV. Months later: the rains end, the station is rebuilt, Dez recovers and stays on as mechanic, Okonjo earns his pilot's papers. Beat: the found family, settled rather than scattered.

chapters.title: What Marguerite Measures
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite installs a new anemometer at the station and, for the first time, keeps a calendar instead of an odometer. Voss's trial begins downstream; she declines to attend. Beat: the theme resolved in quiet action.

chapters.title: A Wreck for the Escarpment
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The inquiry publishes; the escarpment is declared protected. Ilse and Marguerite mark the Tern's wreck site with a buoy, a small ceremony on the water. Beat: honoring what was lost to arrive where they are.

chapters.title: The Next Season's Storm
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A year on, the first storm of the season rolls in and the station's crew watches it together, instruments humming, nowhere to flee. Marguerite stays to watch it land. Beat: the ending—rooted, watching weather instead of outrunning it.
